headline: Power crisis: Shops and malls must close by 8pm nationwide
summary: The government has tightened electricity conservation measures, ordering all shops, markets, and billboards to shut down earlier to save power.
details: Shopping malls, markets, and shops across Bangladesh must now close by 8:00pm to conserve electricity amid the ongoing power crisis.
According to a directive from the Power Division, these establishments can operate from 11:00am to 8:00pm, moving the closing time up from the previous 9:00pm limit.
The government has also ordered all lit billboards to be switched off by 7:00pm, while decorative lighting must remain off at all times.
These restrictions extend to all ongoing and upcoming fairs and cultural programmes, which are now required to end by 8:00pm.
However, essential services including hospitals, pharmacies, and restaurants are exempt from these new closing time restrictions.

headline: Trishal UNO assaults employee during sand mine raid
summary: CCTV footage shows Upazila Nirbahi Officer Arafat Siddique slapping and hitting a managery employee during a mobile court operation in Mymensingh.
details: Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Arafat Siddique has been accused of assaulting a staff member of a sand mine leaseholder in Trishal, Mymensingh. The incident occurred during a mobile court raid on Wednesday afternoon at a sand mine in the Kalirbazar area of Kathal Union.

CCTV footage reveals the UNO entering the office and demanding documents. When the manager, Sarwar Jahan, asked for the identification of the raiding team, the UNO allegedly slapped him and later hit him several times with a stick.

The Assistant Commissioner (Land) was seen attempting to stop the UNO during the assault. Following the incident, the victim was reportedly taken away in a RAB vehicle and later admitted to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital for treatment.

The leaseholder, Shamsuzzaman Masud, stated that the employee was assaulted without any opportunity to present the documents. He claimed that the administration officials eventually left after the lease's validity was confirmed through the verification of papers.
Mymensingh Deputy Commissioner Saifur Rahman said he has seen the video and promised that necessary action will be taken if the victim files a written complaint.
Local residents have called for a neutral investigation into the incident as the viral video sparked widespread discussion and criticism on social media.
caption:
A viral CCTV video shows a government official slapping and hitting an employee during a raid. Who is responsible?

Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Arafat Siddique has been accused of assaulting a staff member of a sand mine leaseholder in Trishal, Mymensingh. The incident occurred during a mobile court raid on Wednesday afternoon at a sand mine in the Kalirbazar area of Kathal Union.

CCTV footage reveals the UNO entering the office and demanding documents. When the manager, Sarwar Jahan, asked for the identification of the raiding team, the UNO allegedly slapped him and later hit him several times with a stick.

The Assistant Commissioner (Land) was seen attempting to stop the UNO during the assault. Following the incident, the victim was reportedly taken away in a RAB vehicle and later admitted to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital for treatment.

The leaseholder, Shamsuzzaman Masud, stated that the employee was assaulted without any opportunity to present the documents. He claimed that the administration officials eventually left after the lease's validity was confirmed through the verification of papers.

Mymensingh Deputy Commissioner Saifur Rahman said he has seen the video and promised that necessary action will be taken if the victim files a written complaint.

Local residents have called for a neutral investigation into the incident as the viral video sparked widespread discussion and criticism on social media.
